referenceCamera.note: Material swatch maps directly to one 8 m UV square; no perspective to solve.

objectClass.notes: Explicit one-quad paving; all small flush aggregate and thin divider detail belongs to material channels.

reasoning: One prescribed plane with a regular divider grid, small exposed pebbles and shallow roughness.

specDepthDecision.rationale: One quad and one PBR material. Review square grid registration, varied aggregate and low surface relief.

detailInventory.scanMethod: full swatch plus original independent PBR strip; eight panels across each axis

details.description: Cream, tan, pale ochre, brown and grey small stones are densely mixed across each panel.
Small rounded and irregular oval pebbles sit flush within a cement matrix.
Thin straight divider strips form eight square panels across the 8 m swatch.
Narrow darker cement spaces separate adjacent pebbles without deep open sett joints.
Warm pale divider strips have a narrow dark edge and slight weathering.
Some square panels have subtly warmer, paler or darker overall aggregate mixtures.
Fine grain and small pores occur within the exposed stone and cement surfaces.
The small exposed pebble crowns read worn and low rather than tall cobblestones.
Sparse brown and olive weathered patches appear around some strips and aggregates.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: Preserve explicit 8 m quad at y=0 with two triangles, one material and no individual pebble geometry.
Preserve dense warm mineral speckle, fine shallow relief and thin square divider strips at 1 m panel pitch.
Use independent PBR channels, with no candy-coat or metallic interpretation.
Four-way rotated neighboring tiles retain panel-grid alignment and no major lighting boundary.
All runtime, resource, collision and export checks pass; reviewed whole-asset score exceeds 95.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.
